comparisons.interpretation: Espinosa and Hernandez each explicitly support Medicare for All or a Medicare-for-All-style universal system. The comparison is timing-unverified because Espinosa's retained archive is dated June 3, one day after the shared-ballot primary.
Espinosa and Samadzadeh each explicitly support a Medicare-for-All single-payer system. Publication and pre-primary timing remain unresolved for the retained platform wording.

Espinosa and Irwin each support accelerating a transition toward renewable or clean energy. The short excerpts do not establish identical timelines, technologies, or labor standards, and both retained wordings are timing-unverified.

Espinosa and Kacker selected the same survey proposition: complete background cleanup removing all man-made contamination or equivalent. The survey's publication date and pre-primary text version remain unresolved.

Pasquarella and Bacon each support extending Medicare coverage to everyone. This is the narrower shared proposition established by the excerpts; Bacon's wording does not by itself establish single-payer financing or identical system design. Bacon's platform launch is dated before the primary; Pasquarella's retained campaign page is undated, so the pair remains timing-unverified.

Pasquarella emphasizes Medicare coverage for everyone, while Carbajal's retained page emphasizes ACA premium-tax-credit expansion to lower premiums. Carbajal's source does not state whether he supports or opposes Medicare for All or single-payer financing, so this is only a difference in the emphasis of the retained passages, not a proven insurance-strategy disagreement. Both retained campaign pages are timing-unverified.
